title: Luxury Brands Slow Down Their Price Increases

source.author: Julia Garel
source.title: Study: Can luxury brands still raise their prices?
source.checked_against: Single source. Web search on 2026-11-13 found no second outlet carrying the November 2026 Retviews by Lectra study; earlier Retviews reports (2023-2025) describe the same pattern (China the most expensive market, gap with Europe narrowing) but give no figures for 2026, so no figure was cross-checked or taken from them. Author and publication date come from the page metadata (the page shows no byline). The article notes it was partly written with an AI tool and then fact-checked and edited by a FashionUnited journalist.

figures.text: study is price tracking by Retviews, Lectra's market analysis solution
figures.quote: These findings come from price tracking compiled by Retviews, Lectra's market analysis solution, unveiled this Thursday.

figures.text: about 80% of luxury market growth between 2023 and 2025 came from price increases, not volume (BoF/McKinsey)
figures.quote: approximately 80 percent of luxury market growth between 2023 and 2025 came from price increases rather than volume.

figures.text: Prada Cleo bag: 1,847 dollars in 2021 to 3,001 dollars in 2026, up 62%
figures.quote: Prada's Cleo bag rose from 1,847 dollars in 2021 to 3,001 dollars in 2026, a 62 percent increase.

figures.text: several brands moved from two price increases a year to one for iconic handbags, since 2025
figures.quote: Several brands have shifted from two price increases per year to just one for their iconic handbags.

figures.text: 18% of luxury executives plan price increases above 5% in 2026, against 26% for fashion as a whole
figures.quote: 18 percent of them plan price increases above 5 percent in 2026, compared to 26 percent for the fashion sector as a whole.

figures.text: five brands compared across markets, Europe as benchmark
figures.quote: Retviews compared the prices charged across several markets by five brands against those in Europe, which serves as the benchmark.

figures.text: China the most expensive market for each of the five brands in 2026
figures.quote: As a result, China remains the most expensive market for each of them in 2026.

figures.text: China vs Europe, average: Miu Miu 50% more, Burberry 45%, Loewe and Prada 40%, Chloé 34%
figures.quote: A Miu Miu product costs an average of 50 percent more there than in Europe.

figures.text: Prada in China: 54% more than Europe in 2025, 40% more in 2026
figures.quote: At Prada, a product sold in China cost an average of 54 percent more than in Europe in 2025, compared to 40 percent in 2026.

figures.text: Japan the only market cheaper than Europe for several houses: Miu Miu 7% less, Burberry and Loewe 5% less
figures.quote: Japan is the only market where several houses sell for less than in Europe, notably Miu Miu (7 percent less), Burberry and Loewe (5 percent less).

figures.text: brands spacing out increases, narrowing gaps between markets, strengthening more accessible offerings
figures.quote: They are also narrowing price gaps between markets and strengthening their more accessible offerings.

figures.text: report links the changes to buyer expectations: emotional connection and identity, not social status alone
figures.quote: desire for luxury brands is increasingly based on emotional connection and identity expression, rather than social status alone.
